newsitem.title: UK: IBCA cuts individual ratings of three Korean banks.
newsitem.headline: IBCA cuts individual ratings of three Korean banks.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Wednesday it had downgraded the individual ratings of Korea First Bank (KFB), Cho Hung Bank (Cho Hung) and Korea Exchange Bank (KEB).
The ratings have been under rating watch since January 24, 1997 following the collapse of Hanbo Iron & Steel Co, IBCA said in a statement.
"KFB's individual rating has been downgraded to D/E from C/D. Both Cho Hung and KEB have been downgraded to C/D from C," IBCA said.
IBCA said the final losses connected with Hanbo were not fixed at this stage, because the future of the Tangjin steel mill project, the core part of the company's assets, was not yet clear.

"In IBCA's view there is little doubt about the Korean government's commitment to resolving the Hanbo crisis in order to avoid widespread damage to the economy and its fiancial system," the agency said.

IBCA said it was most likely that the banks' direct loan losses would be limited by the completion, rather than the abandonment of the project and for most of the lender banks the problem was manageable.

"However, the negative impact of loan loss provisions and loss of interest will give significant pressure of their profitability, not only for the current fiscal year, but for a long period," IBCA said.
IBCA said KFB had suffered the largest impact from the Hanbo crisis.

"Not only does KFB have the largest exposure to Hanbo but also the largest uncollateralised share. Even if the Tangjin project is completed, the impact on KFB's financial condition will be considerable," the agency said. "The downgrading of KFB also reflects its exposure to Sammi Steel, which also failed today."

"For Cho Hung and KEB, the problem is more manageable, because of their smaller share of loans," IBCA said. "Cho Hung's relatively strong growth in its core retail business is expected to absorb a large part of the expected losses, while in the case of KEB its below average burden of the existing problem loans and exposure to the stock market are the positive factors."
IBCA said it was lowering the ratings of these two banks to reflect both the impact of Hanbo, and the general deterioration in their operating environment.
IBCA also mentioned the failure of Sammi Corporation and Sammi Steel, the main companies of Sammi Group, the 28th largest Chaebol (industrial conglomerate) in Korea.

"The company has applied for the legal management (similar to court receivership). KFB and Commercial Bank of Korea (CBK) reportedly have exposures of KRW450 bln and KRW250 bln respectively to Sammi Group and IBCA plans to make a detailed analysis of the impact of this case in its annual review of the Korean banks in April," the agency said.
